llm_calls.reasoning: The alert is a fast-burn ErrorBudgetBurn on checkout, with a 33% error ratio over 5m and no other open incidents. Checkout calls many services, so the root cause may be a dependency. I'm giving each investigator a starting point to determine whether the fault is in checkout or downstream.
Start broad: compare error ratio and p95 latency for checkout and its callers/callees, plus checkout's client span error rates by dependency.

Step 1 shows checkout's error ratio climbing to 0.38 and checkout's client Charge spans to payment returning STATUS_CODE_ERROR (~0.08 to 0.095), while payment's own server latency fell back to ~2 ms. Next I need payment's server-side view (is payment itself erroring for everyone?) and the per-status breakdown of payment server spans, plus checkout's error ratio on the 1m vs 30m windows to date the onset.

Step 2 shows checkout's client Charge spans to payment returning STATUS_CODE_ERROR (about 0.21 to 0.25 per second) starting around 07:46, while payment's own server Charge spans show no ERROR series. One more check: payment server spans by status_code over a short window, and checkout client Charge errors on a 1m window, to confirm whether payment itself is failing.

Payment's server spans show no ERROR series while checkout's client Charge spans show STATUS_CODE_ERROR at about 0.21-0.25/s since about 07:46, so the fault may sit between checkout and payment or in checkout itself. Next I'll check which checkout server endpoints fail and whether checkout shows restarts or CPU throttling.

Metrics localize the errors to checkout's client Charge calls to payment, but payment's own server spans show no errors. I had no step left to check logs, traces for exception messages, rollout history, or flags, so the root cause is not confirmed.
Starting with checkout error logs and Jaeger error spans over the last 15 minutes, as the brief says. I'll run them in parallel, then drill into whichever downstream dependency fails most.

Checkout's error logs are empty, but its error spans all show PaymentService/Charge failing with a dial i/o timeout to 10.96.121.205:9999. Next I'll check payment's own logs and error traces, and search checkout logs for the dial error text.

Checkout's error spans all point at a failed gRPC dial to payment at 10.96.121.205:9999 (i/o timeout), while payment itself shows no error logs or error spans. Next I'll pull the full failing trace, check for payment Charge spans, and search checkout logs for the dial error to see whether the failure is on the network or endpoint side. Retrying with the correct action schema.

Checkout's error spans all trace to failed gRPC dials to payment at 10.96.121.205:9999 (i/o timeout), while payment shows no error logs or error spans and does not appear in any span set. Next I check payment's unfiltered logs and Charge spans in both payment and checkout to see whether payment is receiving the calls at all.

Checkout's error spans consistently show failed gRPC dials to PaymentService at 10.96.121.205:9999 (i/o timeout), while payment shows no error logs or error spans. I did not check rollout history, flags, or Kubernetes endpoints, so the cause of the unreachable address remains open.
Starting broad: checkout's rollout history, recent k8s warning events across otel-demo, and flag states. Then I'll diff any recent revisions and check dependencies.

Checkout revision 2 was created at 07:44:30Z, about 2 minutes before the alert opened, with change cause "payment client moved to port 9999". No flags are on and no warning events hit checkout or payment. Next I'll diff revisions 1 and 2 to confirm the port change, and check payment's own rollout history to see whether its port changed.

The checkout revision 2 diff changes PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999, rolled out at 07:44:30Z, about 2 minutes before the alert. Payment has not changed (single revision from 07:32:06Z), and no warning events or flag changes appear. I have no metrics or trace tools, so I can't confirm payment's listening port or checkout's payment client errors directly; that remains a hypothesis to verify.

Checkout revision 2 changed PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999 two minutes before the alert, and checkout's Charge calls fail with dial timeouts to payment:9999 while payment itself shows no errors and no traffic after 07:44:28Z. The likely fix is to revert checkout's PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:8080, after confirming payment's listening port and Service.

The diagnosis cites checkout revision 2 (07:44:30Z) as the only config change, setting PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999 while payment listens on 8080, and checkout's Charge errors are dial timeouts to 9999. Payment is unchanged since 07:32 and shows no errors. Rolling checkout back to revision 1 restores payment:8080, so I'll propose that directly.

result.report_summary: Checkout rolled out revision 2 at 07:44:30Z, about 2 minutes before the alert, changing its payment address from port 8080 to 9999. Payment has not changed since 07:32:06Z, and no warning events or flags are active. The timing and content fit a checkout-to-payment connection break, though I could not verify payment's port or checkout's client-side errors with my tools.

Checkout's failures are client-side dial timeouts to payment (10.96.121.205:9999, i/o timeout) on PaymentService/Charge. Payment emits no errors and no error spans, and its last log line is at 07:44:28Z, about 2.5 minutes before the alert opened, so payment looks unreachable rather than erroring. Checkout is a symptom-surfacer; the fault is on the payment path or in the network/service address. I did not check changes or flags.

Checkout's availability errors trace to its client calls to PaymentService/Charge, which began returning STATUS_CODE_ERROR around 07:45:55Z. Checkout's 5m error ratio climbed to 0.38. Payment's own server spans show no error series and its p95 latency is about 2 ms, so payment looks healthy from its side. Payment is the likely dependency but not confirmed as the cause; I did not check logs, traces, or rollout/flag changes.

actions.reason: Checkout revision 2 (07:44:30Z) changed PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999. Checkout's Charge calls time out dialing 9999, while payment is unchanged and healthy on 8080. Rolling back to revision 1 restores payment:8080.

alternatives.why_not: A restart keeps the same pod template, so PAYMENT_ADDR stays on 9999 and the timeouts continue.
Checkout is not short of capacity. Its pods are not restarting, and the failures are config-driven dial timeouts, not load.

plan.summary: Roll checkout back to revision 1, which restores PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:8080 and ends the Charge dial timeouts. After the rollback, checkout's error ratio should fall from about 33% toward zero within a few minutes.

facts.statement: Checkout revision 2 (created 07:44:30Z, change-cause 'payment client moved to port 9999') changed PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999. It is the only config difference from revision 1.
Payment has only revision 1 (created 07:32:06Z) and has not changed since.
Checkout's Charge errors are all 'dial tcp 10.96.121.205:9999: i/o timeout'. All 20 sampled checkout error traces contain this, and PlaceOrder carries it too.
Checkout's error logs are empty; the failures show only in trace spans.
Payment has no error logs or error spans. Its last log is at 07:44:28Z, and it has no Charge spans in the window.

Checkout's error ratio rose from 0.23 to 0.38. Checkout's client Charge errors and its server PlaceOrder errors both begin at about 07:45:55Z. Payment's server spans show only UNSET, with p95 about 2 ms.
No feature flags are on, and no warning events involve checkout or payment. Checkout pods are not restarting.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Run kubectl get svc payment -n otel-demo and check that 10.96.121.205 is payment's ClusterIP with port 9999 absent. Check payment's container port and that it listens on 8080.
hypotheses.statement: Payment listens on 8080 and its Service exposes 8080, so 9999 has no listener. The change is wrong, not the network.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check checkout's trace timestamps for the first Charge dial failure after 07:44:30Z, and the client timeout settings.
hypotheses.statement: Onset of client errors (07:45:55Z) is about 85 s after the rollout (07:44:30Z). This may be connection or timeout caching, or a long dial timeout, and it does not change the diagnosis.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Query checkout p95 and traces around 07:34Z to see whether it is an unrelated event.
hypotheses.statement: Frontend's earlier p95 spike at about 07:34Z is separate from this incident and was not investigated.

inferences.statement: The port change is the cause. Checkout's calls to payment:9999 time out, and payment receives nothing, which explains its silence after 07:44:28Z. Payment's healthy metrics are consistent with this.
Frontend's 500s and its low error ratio are downstream of checkout. Checkout is the service to fix, not frontend or payment.

root_causes.cause: Config release revision 2 set PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999 (was payment:8080). Checkout cannot dial payment on 9999, so every Charge call times out and checkout returns failed PlaceOrder requests. Revert the env var to payment:8080 or roll back to revision 1.

Payment is not the root cause, since it has no errors and is unchanged. The alternative would be a payment Service or endpoint issue making 10.96.121.205 unreachable, which is unverified and less likely given the exact timing with checkout's port change.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout's availability burn (about 33% of PlaceOrder requests failing) is caused by checkout's own rollout at 07:44:30Z (revision 2), which changed PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999. Checkout's Charge calls fail with 'dial tcp 10.96.121.205:9999: i/o timeout', and payment shows no errors and no Charge spans after about 07:44:28Z, so checkout never reaches payment's handler. Payment is unchanged since 07:32 and is healthy on its own side. Fix: revert checkout to payment:8080 (or otherwise point it at payment's real port), then confirm the error ratio drops. Flags and resources are not implicated.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: Checkout revision 2 (created 2026-10-28T07:44:30Z, change cause 'checkout config release: payment client moved to port 9999') changed env PAYMENT_ADDR from 'payment:8080' to 'payment:9999'. This is the only config difference from revision 1.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: The payment Deployment has not changed: it has only revision 1, created 2026-10-28T07:32:06Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-payment, with no change cause. So the port change came from checkout alone.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: Checkout's new pod (checkout-6f48f6dcc5-vd4qn) was scheduled and started at 07:44:30-07:44:31Z, replacing the revision 1 pod. The rollout completed with 1/1 ready replicas, so the bad config is live and no pod failed to start.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: Checkout's port move to 9999 is the likely cause of the checkout error rise. Payment's port is most likely still 8080, so checkout's calls to payment:9999 would be refused or time out, and checkout would surface these as its own failed requests. Confirm with checkout's client spans to payment (errors such as connection refused) and payment's listening port.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: No warning events in otel-demo in the last 120 minutes involve checkout or payment; the only warnings are readiness probe failures on alertmanager, otel-collector-agent and loki. No feature flags are on (18 flags, all at default off), so flags do not explain the alert.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: checkout service:sli_error_ratio:rate5m rose from 0.23 at 07:45:32Z to 0.38 at 07:47:02Z (peak); frontend stayed low at about 0.015 to 0.022.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Checkout's client spans to oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge began returning STATUS_CODE_ERROR at about 0.21 to 0.46 per second starting 07:45:55Z, while the UNSET series stayed around 0.0 to 0.3 per second.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Checkout's server PlaceOrder STATUS_CODE_ERROR series started at 07:45:55Z (peak 0.458/s), matching the onset of checkout's payment Charge client errors.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Payment's server spans for Charge show only STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series) through 07:47:15Z, and payment's p95 latency is about 1.9 ms. Payment does not appear to be failing as seen from its own side.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: The fault is localized to the checkout-to-payment path, but not proven. Payment's server metrics show no errors even though checkout sees Charge errors. The cause could be in checkout's client handling, the network path, or payment-side errors that do not show in its server spans. Exception messages in traces or logs are needed to tell these apart.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Checkout's p95 latency spiked to 732 ms around 07:34Z and fell back to about 48 ms. That earlier spike is separate from the current error burst.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: No checkout pod restarts in the 30-minute window (no series returned), so a crash loop does not explain the errors. Rollout history, flag state, logs, and traces were not checked.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Checkout's error logs are empty over the last 15 minutes; the failures appear only in trace spans, not in checkout's logs.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Checkout's error spans all trace to PaymentService/Charge failing with 'connection error: transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 10.96.121.205:9999: i/o timeout'. This appears 20 times in the sampled 20 error traces, and checkout PlaceOrder carries the same error 20 times.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Of the 20 sampled checkout-error traces, all 20 contain the Charge dial failure, and frontend's POST /api/checkout returns 500 for 36 to 40 spans. The downstream symptom is consistent across both samples.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Payment shows no error logs and no error spans in the 15-minute window. Its only logs are 50 'Charge request received.' and 50 'Transaction complete.' lines, the last at 07:44:28Z, while the alert opened at 07:46:48Z.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Payment has no error spans and no Charge spans in the window (zero error spans among 20 sampled traces), so the calls never reach payment's handler. This is consistent with payment being unreachable from checkout.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Checkout's config at startup points payment at paymentSvcAddr 'payment:9999'. The dial target 10.96.121.205:9999 is an IP, so DNS or Service resolution or endpoints for payment, or a network policy, may be the fault. I did not verify that 10.96.121.205 is payment's ClusterIP.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Checked but not run: payment rollout history, feature flags, and Kubernetes events. Whether a recent change caused the payment unreachability is unknown.
